summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, bipolar disorder, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for recurrent severe abdominal pain following a fatty meal and a viral illness. He reported episodes of passing out attributed to pain, which were evaluated and determined to be likely pseudoseizures. Imaging showed no acute intracranial or thoracic abnormalities. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control, anti-nausea medication, and gradual advancement to a low-fat diet. His symptoms improved, he tolerated oral intake, and he was discharged home with a short supply of pain medication, stool softeners, and instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and gastroenterologist.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
